messages.content: Translate the complete CURRENT legal source into a FEW executable semantic constructor expressions. Output operative disclosure permissions/prohibitions and any definitions needed to interpret them. Do not reproduce the source as text records. Expressions use the acquired constructor names as functions with positional arguments; nest calls directly. A zero-argument constructor is NAME(). Text arguments use ordinary ASCII quote delimiters and describe only source-supported names or qualifications. Prefer short exact source wording; canonical descriptions must preserve its exact meaning. Never import an old example participant, purpose or condition. Each statement cites all current span IDs supporting that coherent interpretation. A definition may be a separate statement used by a referring norm. No native answer labels, raw-text roots, Python variables, assignments or imports. There is no literal operator and no model-written node numbering. If no supported interpretation is available, return statements:[]; unknown must not become a negative fact. Distinguish information descriptions, permissions, restrictions, the acting party, recipient ownership, definition references and exception scope. Preserve nested ownership and locally bound references in the tree. Do not infer a permission from a role mention or copy every operator into the output. Use only supported operators; leave unresolved interpretations absent rather than inventing facts. The examples/productions describe a learned translation language: {ARG0:Type} in a source_pattern and ARG0,ARG1 in templates denote typed grammar slots. In your final expressions replace them with actual constructor expressions or current-source strings. Old example facts are not current facts.
